clue.text: Does retired Tadcaster referee keep one in his trousers?

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the concealed letters are read backwards
the two words keep the answer within them, spanning the end of one and the start of the other

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Tadcaster and the start of referee

explanation.surface: A curious question about what a Yorkshire match official keeps down his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses the letters TERREF hidden by 'keep' in 'Tadcaster referee'. Ferret-legging is a Yorkshire pub contest of keeping a live ferret inside your trousers; Tadcaster is a Yorkshire brewing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferret-legging contestants put the animal down their trousers, so a ferret is the creature one might find there.

clue.text: Yen to visit Ireland — looking up a remote place to stay

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the whole is reversed
a visitor goes into a place, so the yen letter is put inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: Someone longing to holiday in Ireland is searching for an out-of-the-way place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to visit' puts Y inside EIRE to give EIRYE, and 'looking up' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest high on a crag, and figuratively any lofty, isolated dwelling.

clue.text: Like a safe investment of crude oil, multiple diamonds, houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside, so the anagram goes within the diamonds

parts.note: rocks is slang for diamonds and D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, so two lots of diamonds

indicators.note: crude oil is unrefined, so the letters of oil are taken in a rough, rearranged form

explanation.surface: Describes a dependable portfolio of crude oil and a stash of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Multiple' is why two diamond words are needed: the slang one and the card-suit letter. 'crude' rearranges the oil, and 'houses' sets it between the two diamond pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means utterly reliable and secure, which is what a safe investment is.

clue.text: Gift story books

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Story books given as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in the sense of a natural ability is a talent.

clue.text: Bin fish stew accompaniment

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away, to dump it
a ling is a long-bodied fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A cook throws out the fish meant for a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bin' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumplings are balls of dough traditionally cooked in and served with a stew.

clue.text: Overcharging daft Big Brother lad year in, year out

indicators.note: in here means the first year letter goes inside the rearranged letters
daft means silly or crazy, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

parts.note: Y is the standard abbreviation for year, and out says this one stays outside, at the end

explanation.surface: A reality-show contestant is accused of ripping people off, year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daft' rearranges BIG BROTHER LAD into DALIGHTROBBER; 'in' puts one Y inside it, after DA, and with 'year out' the other Y stays outside, at the end. Big Brother is a TV reality show.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight robbery is the idiom for charging a blatantly excessive price.

clue.text: Mum runs over solemn German nobleman

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the next one

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mum
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
grave means solemn or serious

explanation.surface: A mother hurries past a sombre German aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a hereditary title of German nobility, originally a lord governing a border province.

clue.text: 1st of last month, old copper drafted in as stand-in

indicators.note: something drafted in is brought into a team, so these letters go inside the others
1st of picks the opening letter of the word last

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: On the first of last month, a retired policeman was brought in to cover for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal. 'drafted in' puts O + CU between L and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily covers for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Bath dandy left boring, vulgar city

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous 18th-century dandy and master of ceremonies at Bath

indicators.note: boring here means drilling into, so the left letter goes inside the word for vulgar

parts.note: vile can mean base or vulgar

explanation.surface: A dandy from Bath found a crude city tedious and left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but means piercing. Bath is an elegant spa city in England, where Beau Nash ruled society.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital city of Tennessee, famous for country music.

clue.text: Labourer paid for a bonding session?

definitions.text: Labourer paid for a bonding session?

parts.words: Labourer paid for a bonding session?
parts.note: bonding is the pattern in which bricks are laid to tie a wall together, so the worker paid for it is the one laying them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonding session' suggests a team-building event, but in building, bond is the arrangement of bricks in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a tradesman who lays bricks in a bond pattern to build walls.

clue.text: Intimate company escorting son

indicators.note: an escort surrounds the person protected, so the company letters go around the son letter

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm accompanies a son, keeping things close.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy describes a snug, friendly, close atmosphere, as an intimate setting is.

clue.text: Sheik bust with nil capital

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheik goes broke and is left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as bankrupt, but it signals breaking the letters of SHEIK and NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Dismiss class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... someone from office is to dismiss them
second meaning: a form or class in some British schools

explanation.walkthrough: In some British public schools the Remove is the name of a particular year group or form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for sacking someone and a noun naming a school form.

clue.text: Whimper, sounding like a cross animal

indicators.note: sounding like says the answer is pronounced the same as the word for the animal

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: An angry beast whimpering pitifully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests angry, but it means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to cry feebly, like a baby, which is a whimper.

clue.text: It's used to soothe little Mary when visiting hospital department

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the girl's name is placed within the department letters

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
Mollie is a pet form of the name Mary

explanation.surface: Something to calm a small girl named Mary when she goes to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a cream or preparation that softens and calms the skin.

clue.text: Waspish type hot cycling elevated roadway

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round, the first three moving from the front to the back

parts.note: a flyover is a road carried over another on a bridge

explanation.surface: A hot, irritable cyclist on a raised road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves FLY from the front of FLYOVER to the back, giving OVERFLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoverfly is an insect whose yellow and black stripes mimic a wasp.

clue.text: Italian leaves wireless receiving Chic broadcast

indicators.note: receiving means the radio takes the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: wireless is an old word for a radio

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian walks away while the radio picks up a programme by the band Chic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, but it means foliage. 'broadcast' rearranges CHIC as ICCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved Italian chicory used in salads.

clue.text: Oil carrier bound for north-west Africa heading north an hour away

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means the letters run upwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: bound for means heading to, so it gives the word to

indicators.note: away says the hour letter is removed

parts.note: the Maghreb is the region of north-west Africa
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A tanker sailing to north-west Africa turns north, an hour late.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping H from TO MAGHREB leaves TOMAGREB, which 'heading north' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot orange carries in its rind the fragrant oil used in Earl Grey tea and perfumes.

clue.text: Cherish husband and elderly partner

parts.note: old means elderly
dear is a term for a loved partner

explanation.surface: Value your husband and your aged partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone dear is the idiom for treasuring or loving them.

clue.text: Extracted natural moisture bordering river

indicators.note: bordering means the moisture word surrounds the river letter

parts.note: dew is moisture that forms naturally overnight

explanation.surface: Water was taken from the dew along a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew is the past tense of draw, to pull out, as in drawing a tooth.

clue.text: Herbal sample infused with busy Lizzie?

indicators.note: the phrase is infused with the answer, which runs through it across the two words

explanation.surface: A herbal tea sample mixed with a garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy Lizzie' looks like a person, but it is the plant; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy Lizzie is a type of Impatiens, the genus of plants commonly called balsams.

clue.text: Yard probing Head of Special Branch, notoriously devious individual

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
probing means poking into, so the yard letters go inside

parts.note: a log is a branch or piece of wood

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard investigates the chief of the police intelligence unit, a famously shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' and 'Special Branch' suggest the police, but Yard is just its abbreviation and Branch is a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly dog is an informal idiom for a cunning or secretive person.

clue.text: Section of River Shannon essentially maintained

parts.note: Del Shannon was the 1960s singer of Runaway, so Shannon gives his first name

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Part of the River Shannon is kept up, in essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Shannon' looks like one name, the Irish river, but Shannon is the singer Del Shannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan-shaped area of deposits at a river's mouth, a part of the river.

clue.text: Irish poet spurning hot dog ultimately preferred tofu

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the hot letter is left out

parts.note: Brendan Behan was an Irish poet and playwright
a cur is a dog, usually a mongrel

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of preferred

explanation.surface: An Irish poet turns down a hot dog and in the end opts for tofu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dog' reads as a snack but splits into H and CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is made by curdling soya milk, which is why it is also called bean curd.

clue.text: Compact powder tip of garden rake buries

indicators.note: buries means the word for rake holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A garden rake's tip pushes something into the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool, but it is a debauched man, a ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is red cosmetic powder, often carried in a make-up compact.

clue.text: Meat which can be bought with the heart removed

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, which is taken away

parts.note: venal means open to bribery, able to be bought

explanation.surface: Meat on sale with its heart cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: VENAL loses its middle letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the meat of a calf.

clue.text: Travelling each summer, it can get piping hot!

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Going abroad every summer, it gets scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piping hot' sounds like hot food, but it means a hot pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerschaum is a soft white clay used to carve tobacco pipes, which heat up when smoked.

clue.text: Ransack stately home, initially breaking in like a cat burglar

indicators.note: breaking in means the home letter forces its way inside the others
to ransack is to turn things upside down, so the letters are jumbled
initially points to the first letter of home

explanation.surface: A burglar raids a stately home, breaking in quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ransack' rearranges STATELY into STEALTY, and 'breaking in' puts H inside, before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat burglar works furtively and quietly, so stealthy describes how one moves.

clue.text: Secured weepie co-star for Swayze, P?

parts.note: Demi Moore starred opposite Patrick Swayze in the tear-jerker film Ghost
Swayze, P is surname then initial, so on that pattern his co-star's initial, D for Demi, follows her surname

explanation.surface: Asks who Patrick Swayze's tearjerker co-star was, in a register-style name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swayze, P' gives the format, surname then initial, so his Ghost co-star Demi Moore becomes MOORE, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is moored is tied up and made fast at a berth.
